paras: The Ash Fork shooting of a fleeing Black man by officers took place on a Sunday evening in August 1910, probably 21 August, at Ash Fork, Arizona, when officers chased an unnamed "colored man" and fired a number of shots at him. The man, who was said to have used his revolver on a Mexican, escaped into the foothills, and no injury to him was reported. The only known account is a short paragraph in the Williams News.

The incident came two days after another shooting at Ash Fork, in which Enrique Barajos shot Francisco Basquez five times in a quarrel over a woman. Basquez died at the hospital in Prescott the following Monday evening, and at last accounts Barajos had not been captured.

According to the Williams News, on Sunday evening "a colored man used his six-shooter on a Mexican" at Ash Fork. The paper did not say whether the Mexican was hit, and it stated that it was unable to learn what led to the shooting. Officers at once gave chase and fired "a number of shots at the fleeing negro," but he made his escape into the foothills.
No report of an arrest, a name for either man, or any later proceeding was found in the coverage.

The Williams News printed the incident on 27 August as the closing paragraph of a front-page item headed "Shooting Affrays at Ash Fork," most of which described the Basquez shooting. It identified the man only by race, as "a colored man" and "the fleeing negro," and reported the officers' fire without comment. No second account of the incident, in Arizona papers or elsewhere, was found in the coverage. No Black-press report of the incident was found.

bases: The only report (A4) says officers chased a fleeing Black man accused of using his gun on a Mexican and fired a number of shots at him; no hit is reported.
Only the Williams News (A4) reports the incident; Arizona and New Mexico items on Ash Fork shootings that week (A1, A2, A3, A5) concern a separate Mexican-on-Mexican killing.

accounts.label: Williams News local report
accounts.gist: A colored man used his six-shooter on a Mexican on Sunday evening and escaped into the foothills although officers chased him and fired a number of shots; the paper could not learn the particulars.

framing.detail: Reported as the second of two 'shooting affrays' at Ash Fork, calling the man 'a colored man' and 'the fleeing negro', with no comment on the officers' fire.
